/-!
# Bounds on fractional parts $n r^2 - a(n)$ for $r = (2+\sqrt{5})/2$

$a(n) = \lfloor r \cdot \lfloor r \cdot n \rfloor \rfloor$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.

*References:*
- [A341254](https://oeis.org/A341254)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA341254


open Real

/-- The constant $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$. -/
noncomputable def rConst : ℝ := (2 + sqrt 5) / 2

/-- The constant $r^2$. -/
noncomputable def rSq : ℝ := rConst * rConst

/--
$a(n) = \lfloor r \cdot \lfloor r \cdot n \rfloor \rfloor$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.
Note: The original OEIS definition has $n$ starting at 1. We define $a(n)$ for all $\mathbb{N}$.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let r := rConst
  let inner_floor : ℤ := Int.floor (r * n)
  (Int.floor (r * inner_floor.cast)).toNat


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 4 := by
  unfold a rConst
  dsimp only
  push_cast
  rw [mul_one]
  have h1 : ⌊(2 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2⌋ = 2 := by
    rw [Int.floor_eq_iff]
    have h5 : 2236 / 1000 < Real.sqrt 5 ∧ Real.sqrt 5 < 2237 / 1000 := by
      norm_num [Real.sqrt_lt, Real.lt_sqrt]
    constructor <;> linarith
  rw [h1]
  push_cast
  have h2 : ⌊(2 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2 * 2⌋ = 4 := by
    rw [Int.floor_eq_iff]
    have h5 : 2236 / 1000 < Real.sqrt 5 ∧ Real.sqrt 5 < 2237 / 1000 := by
      norm_num [Real.sqrt_lt, Real.lt_sqrt]
    constructor <;> linarith
  rw [h2]
  rfl

/--
Conjecture: $1/4 < n r^2 - a(n) < 3$ for $n \ge 1$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/341254.wip.lean#L188"]
theorem a_bounds (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : (1 / 4 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * rSq - (a n : ℝ) ∧
    (n : ℝ) * rSq - (a n : ℝ) < 3 := by
    sorry

end OeisA341254

findings.description: The module heading calls n*r² − a(n) a “fractional part,” but this quantity is the double-floor error and can exceed 1. For example, a(3)=12 and 3*r²−12 = 3*sqrt(5)−21/4 > 1. The inequality, and consequently the impossibility of this value being any real number's fractional part, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The definitions and theorem statements themselves are correct.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A341254 states “1/4 < n*r^2 - a(n) < 3 for n >= 1”; its June 9, 2026 proof note identifies the fractional part instead as “eps = n*r - floor(n*r).” Read through https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A341/A341254.seq. The A341254 row in Appendix A of arXiv:2608.11941 likewise calls n*r²−a(n) the error.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the module heading to “Bounds on the double-floor error $n r^2 - a(n)$ for $r = (2+\sqrt{5})/2$”. No Lean declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The source uses positive integer indices and an integer double floor. Lean uses n : ℕ with 1 ≤ n, and a natural-valued sequence obtained by applying Int.toNat to the outer floor, with the definition additionally available at zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every natural n, rConst > 0 makes both floor arguments nonnegative, so the outer integer floor is nonnegative. Int.toNat_of_nonneg therefore proves that (a n : ℤ) is exactly the source's double floor. Positive naturals correspond precisely to integers at least 1, and rSq = rConst². Review.bounds_iff_source proves the equivalence of the complete universally quantified statements without using a_bounds. Also, a(0)=0; the theorem correctly excludes that index, where its lower bound would fail.
